subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Mass production has increased the tendency to view things as useful rather than delightful.
P: These various things share nothing with the buttons except money value.
Q: All the rest you wish to exchange for food, shelter, and many other things.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The giant wall of the Dhauladhar range in Himachal Pradesh is one of the most stunning sights in the Himalayas.
P: As the life line of the region it acts as a watershed ridge between Chamba’s Ravi river system and Kangra’s Beas river system.
Q: Although of modest altitude compared to other Himalayan ranges - the highest Dhauladhar peak is less than 5,000 m.

S6: Looming over the hill stations of Dharmsala and McLeodganj, the Dhauladhar is a popular trekking destination.
explanation: QSRP: modest altitude (Q) - despite that, sweeps up 12000 ft (S) - thus the life line (R) - as the life line it is a watershed (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Truth is far more important than the teacher.
P: Without self-knowledge, the airplane becomes the most destructive instrument in life; but with self-knowledge, it is a means of human help.
Q: Wisdom begins with self-knowledge; and without self-knowledge, mere information leads to destruction.

explanation: QRSP: wisdom begins with self-knowledge (Q) - be the perfect teacher, understand yourself (R) - be both pupil and teacher (S) - else the airplane is destructive (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Though most of us talk of discipline, what do we mean by that word ?
P: The teacher would understand each child and help him in the way required.
Q: But if you have five or six in a class, and an intelligent understanding teacher with a warm heart, I am sure there would be no need for discipline.
R: When you have a hundred boys in a class, you will have to have discipline; otherwise there will be complete chaos.
S: Discipline in schools becomes necessary when there is one teacher to a hundred boys and girls.

S6: And most of us are interested in - mass movements, large schools with a great many boys and girls; we are not interested in creative intelligence, therefore we put up huge schools with enormous attendances.
explanation: SRQP: discipline needed when one teacher to a hundred (S) - a hundred boys need discipline (R) - but five or six with a good teacher don't (Q) - the teacher understands each (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Tolstoy Farm was founded in 1910 by which time Gandhi had already conceptualized ideas that he would develop in India.
P: He was rich and used his money to buy the land and help set up the farm.

explanation: SQPR: he put in the moral/religious components (S) - Kallenbach was by his side (Q) - he bought the land (P) - the farm became a subject of research (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Decentralized planning is a process of planning that begins from the | grassroots level taking into confidence all the beneficiaries.

explanation: SRPQ: implemented through market mechanism (S) - empowers individuals (R) - operation is bottom-to-top (P) - more connected with capitalistic economies (Q).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: It is doubtful if mankind, throughout his long history, has ever lived at all ‘sustainably’.
P: But in general mankind has regarded the environment as an endless ‘resource’ to be exploited and plundered.
Q: May be a few isolated tribal groups found the necessary balance with nature lived without the desire for endless ‘more’.
R: Now we have reached a point where we are on the verge of destroying ourselves and most of the life on earth.
S: This process has accelerated greatly since the industrial revolution.
S6: The concept of ‘sustainable’ is so far from reality that it is almost laughable.
explanation: QPSR: a few tribal groups found balance (Q) - but mankind exploited the environment (P) - accelerated since the industrial revolution (S) - now on the verge of destruction (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Measurement is an important concept in performance management.
P: It also indicates where things are not going so well, so that corrective action can be taken.
Q: It identifies where things are going well to provide the foundations for building further success.
R: It is the basis for providing and generating feedback.
S: Measuring performance is relatively easy for those who are responsible for achieving quantified targets for example sales. 1
S6: It is more difficult in the case of knowledge workers for example scientists and teachers.
explanation: PQRS: it indicates where things go badly (P) - identifies where they go well (Q) - basis for feedback (R) - easy for quantified targets (S).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: Equity theory is concerned with the perception people have about how they are being treated compared with others.
P: To be dealt with equitably is to be treated fairly in comparison with another group of people or a relevant other person.
Q: Equity involves feelings and perceptions and is always a comparative process.
R: Equity theory states, in effect, that people will be better motivated if they are treated equitably and demotivated if they are treated inequitably. .
S: It is not synonymous with equality, which means treating everyone the same, since this would be inequitable if they deserve to be treated differently.
S6: This explains only one aspect of the process of motivation and job satisfaction, although it may be significant in terms of morale.
explanation: PQSR: equitable = fair vs others (P) - equity involves feelings, comparative (Q) - not the same as equality (S) - theory: motivated if equitable (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: We cannot understand the power of rumours and prophecies in history by checking whether they are factually correct or not.
P: The rumours in 1857 began to make sense when seen in the context of the policies the British pursued from the late 1820s.
Q: Rumours circulate only when they resonate with the deeper fears and suspicions of people.

R: Under the leadership of Governor General Lord William Bentinck, the British adopted policies aimed at “reforming” Indian society by introducing Western education, Western ideas and Western Institutions.
S: We need to see what they reflect about the minds of people who believed them - their fears and apprehensions, their faiths and convictions.
S6: With the cooperation of sections of Indian society they set up English-medium schools, colleges and universities which taught Western sciences and liberal arts.
explanation: SQPR: see what rumours reflect about people's minds (S) - they resonate with deeper fears (Q) - 1857 rumours made sense in context (P) - Bentinck's reform policies (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The Constitution of India thus emerged through a process of intense debate and discussion.
P: This was an unprecedented act of faith, for in other democracies the vote had been granted slowly, and in stages.
Q: However, on one central feature of the Constitution there was substantial agreement.
R: Many of the provisions were arrived at through a process of give-and-take, by forging a middle ground between two opposed positions.
S: This was on the granting of the vote to every adult Indian.
S6: In countries such as the United States and the United Kingdom, only men with education were allowed into the charmed circle.
explanation: RQSP: provisions arrived at by give-and-take (R) - however, on one feature there was agreement (Q) - granting the vote to every adult (S) - an unprecedented act of faith (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: He no longer dreamed of storms, nor of women, nor of great occurrences, nor of great fish, nor fights, nor contests of strength, nor of his wife.
P: He never dreamed about the boy.
Q: He only dreamed of places and of the lions on the beach now.

S6: He urinated outside the shack and then went up the road to wake the boy.
explanation: QSPR: he dreamed only of places and lions (Q) - they played like cats, loved as the boy (S) - never dreamed of the boy (P) - woke and dressed (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: We do not know, after 60 years of education, how to protect ourselves against epidemics like cholera and plague.

explanation: RQSP: a serious blot that doctors haven't eradicated disease (R) - homes show no hygiene (Q) - graduates don't know snakebite first-aid (S) - if trained earlier (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The weak have no place here, in this life or in any other life. Weakness leads to slavery.
P: They dare not approach us, they have no power to get a hold on us, until the mind is weakened.

explanation: QSRP: weakness is misery/death (Q) - microbes surround us (S) - but can't harm unless we weaken (R) - they dare not approach until the mind weakens (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The Nobel Prize for Economics in 2018 was awarded to Paul Romer and William Nordhaus for their work in two separate areas: economic growth and environmental economics respectively.

explanation: PRQS: a common thread (P) - activity has spillovers (R) - termed externality (Q) - both studied externalities (S).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The climate question presents a leapfrog era for India's development paradigm.

Q: At the Bonn conference, a new Transport Decarbonisation Alliance has been declared.

explanation: SRQP: India has an ambitious renewable policy (S) - must be pursued, rooftop solar (R) - Transport Decarbonisation Alliance at Bonn (Q) - aims at sustainable fuels (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: The dawn of the information age opened up great opportunities for the beneficial use of data.

Q: It also enhanced the perils of unregulated and arbitrary use of personal data.

S: Unauthorised leaks, hacking and other cyber crimes have rendered data bases vulnerable.

S6: To some, in this era of Big Data analytics and automated, algorithm-based processing of zettabytes of information, the fear that their personal data may be unprotected may conjure up visions of a dystopian world in which individual liberties are compromised.
explanation: QSPR: also enhanced perils of data misuse (Q) - leaks/hacking made data vulnerable (S) - conflict of progress vs autonomy (P) - hence the White Paper (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: In a globalised world, no country can hope to impose tariffs without affecting its own economic interests.

explanation: QPSR: tariffs disadvantage consumers, disrupt supply (Q) - so US & China do no good (P) - Fed minutes show US investment hit (S) - China equally affected (R).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: One of the most important forces in the modern world, socialism was a direct result of the Industrial Revolution.

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

explanation: QSRP: they shape preferences/power (Q) - also give order (S) - transformed by the politics they produce (R) - once established, dynamic relationship (P).

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.

subject: Ordering of Sentences

subject: Ordering of Sentences

subject: Ordering of Sentences
directions: Each item consists of six sentences of a passage. S1 and S6 are fixed; the middle four (P, Q, R, S) are jumbled. Choose the proper sequence.
subs: S1: One day her mother, having made some cakes, said to her, "Go, my dear, and see how your grandmother is doing, for I hear she has been very ill. Take her a cake, and this little pot of butter."
